al_omen_area.blurb: Omen Area is a small pocket of boulders within Bishop Mountain, the bouldering zone closest to Huntsville. No trails lead in, so reaching it means picking your own line through the woods. It holds five problems and they run hard: the spread climbs from mid-grade up through the high V-grades, with a couple of problems at the top end of the scale. The centerpiece is a very tall boulder, so bring plenty of pads and a spotter for anything you attempt. The rock here is sandstone. Expect a quiet visit, since this is far from the main clusters on the mountain and is better suited to strong climbers than to beginners.

al_muscle_boulder.blurb: Muscle Boulder is a low block in the middle cluster of Bishop Mountain, the bouldering zone nearest Huntsville. It has a sloping top, and most of its five problems are variations on mantling over that lip. The grades stay friendly, running from V1 up to V4 with a pair each at V1 and V2, which makes it a handy warm-up stop or a place for newer boulderers to practice topping out. The stone is sandstone. Reaching it takes a short hike up to the top of the cliff and then back along it, so it is a bit off the busiest part of the Middle Bishop circuit.

al_sandtrap_the.blurb: The Sandtrap is a small trad sector at Sand Rock (Cherokee Rock Village), a sandstone climbing park in Cherokee County near Leesburg. It sits just beyond the Sun Wall along the base of the cliffline, in a wide sandy clearing. Five trad routes are recorded here, grouped tightly around 5.9 and 5.10, so it suits climbers comfortable leading at that level who want a few quality lines without the crowd of the park's main pinnacles. Sandstone holds can snap, and the rock is best left alone after rain. Sport and trad routes often sit close together elsewhere at Sand Rock, but this clearing is traditional protection only.

al_crow_point.blurb: Crow Point is a compact wall of sport routes inside Little River Canyon National Preserve near Fort Payne. It has five bolted lines, all in the 5.12 range apart from one 5.13 test piece, so this is a crag for experienced climbers rather than a place to learn. The wall is short but steep, and the finishing stretches feel long and exposed. Getting to the base means walking along the cliffline and then scrambling uphill alongside the rock to a ledge system. The canyon's sandstone climbing is described as possible nearly year-round, which makes Crow Point a reasonable stop for a hard project in most seasons.

al_found_boulder.blurb: Found Boulder is a tall block in the middle cluster of Bishop Mountain, the bouldering area closest to Huntsville. Its back side has an unusual roof that blends into a slab, and most of the problems finish at the break. It sits right beside the Lost Boulder. The five problems cover a wide range, from an easy V1 to a pair of problems up around V8, with mid-grade lines between. That mix means a beginner can warm up here while a strong climber has a serious goal on the same stone. The rock is sandstone.

al_the_paw_boulder.blurb: The Paw is one of the boulders in the main cluster at Rainbow Mountain in Madison, close to Huntsville. It stands beside the trail junction on the loop, a short walk in along the trail that passes Balance Rock. Five problems are recorded, mostly easy to moderate: one around V1, a trio near V2, and a single V4 as the hardest. That puts it in the sweet spot for newer boulderers and for a quick after-work session. Rainbow Mountain as a whole is known for easy bouldering with a very short approach from the parking area.

al_turtle_rock_area_corridors_area.blurb: The Corridors Area is a small cluster of boulders in the Turtle Rock section of Horse Pens 40, the well-known sandstone bouldering park near Steele. The problems are found inside a narrow corridor, reached by going around the right side of the big stage. The spot is described as staying in shade all the time, which is useful on warm days. Five problems are recorded, running from V0 through V5 with roughly one at each step, so the grades are friendly for most climbers. Horse Pens 40 itself is best visited in fall and winter, and it is known for sloper-heavy climbing.
